samples.summary: Presence payload shape changed but `docs-presence.md` (the canonical presence doc) is now contradicted and un-updated
samples.evidence: The diff extends the presence wire shape in `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:29-30` (`activeSelection.anchor/focus` now carry `lineAffinity`). The canonical presence design doc still says the opposite: `docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:188` — "For remote cursors, `lineAffinity` is not in the presence payload. Default to `'backward'` ... acceptable for peer display", its `DocsPresence` snippet at :93-95 still shows endpoints as `{ blockId, offset }`, and :381 states "Default `lineAffinity` is `'backward'`, matching peer cursor rendering". Per CONTRIBUTING, a data-model change must update the canonical subsystem doc; instead only `docs-local-caret-anchoring.md` (the Yorkie-anchoring doc) was touched, leaving two design docs in direct conflict about whether affinity is in presence.

samples.summary: Design doc (and the new `DocPosition` doc comment) record a default that the implementation does not use
samples.evidence: The doc paragraph added at docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:80-90 says "it is optional, so a position without one keeps the historical backward reading", and `packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:204-206` repeats "a position that carries no affinity keeps the default backward reading". But `packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260` implements `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` — the shipped default for a selection *start* is forward, not backward, and the new test 'defaults an affinity-less start to the forward reading' asserts exactly that. The design doc therefore misrecords the data-model semantics it was updated to document; the task file itself calls this "a deliberate deviation from the issue's 'keep the backward default' wording" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:20-26), which never made it into the design doc.

samples.summary: Flipping the affinity-less start default to 'forward' is out-of-scope behavior change affecting every other `computeSelectionRects` caller
samples.evidence: The change's own scope statement lists "Changing the default affinity for endpoints that do not carry one" under **Out of scope** (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:63), yet selection.ts:260 changes the default for all callers. `computeSelectionRects` is not selection-only: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1620` (peer selections), :1640 (search highlights), :1659 (comment marker rects, whose output is cached for hit-testing via `commentMarkerRects`), :1676 (spell-error squiggles) and `text-box-editor.ts:560` all pass ranges built from bare `{ blockId, offset }`. The stated justification ("only removes an invisible zero-width rect") is asserted in the lessons file, not verified for these consumers, and the accompanying doc/comment claim the opposite default — so the requested behavior for wrap-boundary endpoints could have been achieved without touching the shared default.

samples.summary: View-level affinity added to the model `DocPosition`, creating a second source of truth next to `Cursor.lineAffinity`
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:13` already owns `lineAffinity` as caret state, and the hit-test helpers already return it as a sibling field (`find-position-at-pixel.ts:18`, `text-editor.ts:4312` uses `DocPosition & { lineAffinity }`). Putting an optional copy on the model type means callers must now keep both in sync by hand (`text-editor.ts:2775-2779` sets `focus.lineAffinity` *and* `cursor.moveTo(newPos, focusAffinity)`), and it pushes view metadata into `packages/docs/src/model`, which the caret-anchoring doc lists under Non-Goals as "Redesigning `DocPosition` throughout `packages/docs`". A selection-endpoint-scoped type (or reusing the existing `DocPosition & { lineAffinity }` intersection already used in text-editor) would keep the layering intact.

samples.summary: Presence caret half of the feature is left inconsistent: `activeCursorPos` type not extended while the store publishes affinity on it
samples.evidence: `updateCursorPos` was widened to accept `lineAffinity` (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:2968`) and publishes `clampedPos` into presence (`:3000` area), but `DocsPresence.activeCursorPos` in `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:19-22` still declares only `{ blockId; offset }`. Only `activeSelection` was extended, so peer caret consumers (`docs-view.tsx:226` `position: p.presence.activeCursorPos!`) cannot see the affinity — the change is half-applied at the presence boundary. Note packages/frontend has no `tsc` lane, so nothing mechanical flags the asymmetry.

samples.summary: Keyboard endpoint affinity applied only to shift+Home; the mirror paths were left untouched
samples.evidence: `handleHome` now attaches `lineAffinity: 'forward'` to the focus (text-editor.ts:2811-2814), but `handleEnd` (:2827) still sets `focus: newPos` with no affinity even though a visual line end is exactly the same wrap-boundary offset, and the double/triple-click paths (:1607, :1616) also build endpoints from a hit without affinity. With the new start default of 'forward', an affinity-less End focus that normalizes into the range *start* now reads forward — the very mis-paint the change is meant to fix. Either the omission is deliberate (then it belongs in the doc's scope note) or the feature is incompletely applied across keyboard endpoints.

samples.summary: Lessons note claims the presence shape is unchanged, but the diff changes it
samples.evidence: The lessons file states extending `DocPosition` "keeps the presence/undo shapes unchanged" (line 15-18), while the same change edits `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:29-30` to add `lineAffinity` to the presence `activeSelection` endpoints. Minor record-keeping inconsistency in the task notes.

finding.summary: Presence payload shape changed but `docs-presence.md` (the canonical presence doc) is now contradicted and un-updated
finding.evidence: The diff extends the presence wire shape in `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:29-30` (`activeSelection.anchor/focus` now carry `lineAffinity`). The canonical presence design doc still says the opposite: `docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:188` — "For remote cursors, `lineAffinity` is not in the presence payload. Default to `'backward'` ... acceptable for peer display", its `DocsPresence` snippet at :93-95 still shows endpoints as `{ blockId, offset }`, and :381 states "Default `lineAffinity` is `'backward'`, matching peer cursor rendering". Per CONTRIBUTING, a data-model change must update the canonical subsystem doc; instead only `docs-local-caret-anchoring.md` (the Yorkie-anchoring doc) was touched, leaving two design docs in direct conflict about whether affinity is in presence.

verdict.reason: Verified both halves myself. The presence wire shape did change: packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:25-30 adds optional lineAffinity to DocsPresence.activeSelection.anchor/focus, and it is really carried through the presence layer (yorkie-doc-store.ts:67, :994-999, :1191-1194, :2968, :2994-3001). The canonical, README-linked presence doc (docs/design/README.md:48 -> docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md) was not updated: its DocsPresence snippet at :88-102 still shows activeSelection endpoints as { blockId, offset }, and a grep for "affinity" in that file returns only the pre-existing remote-cursor lines :188, :381, :503, :569. I searched wide for a counterexample: grep activeSelection across docs/design hits only docs-presence.md; the only doc that documents endpoint affinity is docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:76-90 and :99-106 (DocPosition + AnchoredDocPosition), which the reviewer already acknowledged. That doc IS README-linked (README:55) and IS the doc the task plan designated (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:57-58), so the "no parallel doc / update an existing doc" part of the discipline rule is met — but nothing anywhere documents the presence payload gaining the field, so the specific absence claimed is real. Two caveats that soften the reviewer's framing (hence low confidence on it being blocking rather than a doc nit): docs-presence.md:188 and :381 are about remote *cursors* / activeCursorPos, and users.ts:21-24 still declares activeCursorPos as { blockId, offset }, so those sentences are not literally contradicted; the only concretely stale text is the activeSelection snippet at :93-95 omitting a newly added optional field. I could not find any counterexample that would let me drop this from the gate, so it stays.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence checks out verbatim. docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:80-90 states that "a position without one keeps the historical backward reading" in a paragraph explicitly scoped to selection endpoints (DocRange.anchor/.focus and selection.ts's affinity pass-through), and packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:204-206 repeats "a position that carries no affinity keeps the default backward reading". The shipped implementation is asymmetric: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261 sets `startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (and 'backward' only for the end), applied to both the cell-internal path (line 268) and the block paths; the new test packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts:117 asserts the forward default for an affinity-less start. The task file docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:20-26 records this as "a deliberate deviation from the issue's 'keep the backward default' wording" and its Out-of-scope line 63 still says the default is unchanged; plan step 6 (line 57-58) assigned the design-doc update, but the deviation was never recorded there. So the canonical subsystem design doc and the new data-model doc comment misrecord the semantics they were updated to document. No guard or other doc reconciles them, so there is no named ground to refute; this is a design-doc-discipline/spec mismatch about the data model, not a style or taste preference.

finding.summary: Flipping the affinity-less start default to 'forward' is out-of-scope behavior change affecting every other `computeSelectionRects` caller
finding.evidence: The change's own scope statement lists "Changing the default affinity for endpoints that do not carry one" under **Out of scope** (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:63), yet selection.ts:260 changes the default for all callers. `computeSelectionRects` is not selection-only: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1620` (peer selections), :1640 (search highlights), :1659 (comment marker rects, whose output is cached for hit-testing via `commentMarkerRects`), :1676 (spell-error squiggles) and `text-box-editor.ts:560` all pass ranges built from bare `{ blockId, offset }`. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed: selection.ts:260 sets `startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` inside `buildRects`, the shared code path for every `computeSelectionRects` caller (selection.ts:722). This changes the default for endpoints that carry no affinity, which the change's own task doc lists under Out of scope (todo.md:63) — while acceptance criterion 4 (todo.md:18-26) self-describes it as a deliberate deviation from the issue's "keep the backward default" wording, so the artifacts contradict each other. The design doc updated by this change states the opposite behavior ("a position without one keeps the historical backward reading", docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:83-84, repeated at :90), so the doc and the shipped default disagree. The affected non-selection consumers are real and pass bare `{blockId, offset}` ranges: editor.ts:1620 (peer selections), :1638-1651 (search highlights), :1656-1669 (comment markers cached in `commentMarkerRects` for hit-testing), :1676-1687 (spell errors), and text-box-editor.ts:560. No guard restricts the new default to selection endpoints. Under the design-fit rubric this is a stated-non-goal/scope violation plus a design-doc mismatch — major, not refutable.
